q: Which figure is used to start or stop fluid flow in a major water line?
n: A gate valve (Figure A) gives full on/off control on main lines.

q: Which figure is also known as a sluice valve?
n: A gate valve is also called a sluice valve.

q: Which figure is commonly used to connect to a water closet?
n: An angle valve (Figure D) feeds the water closet.

q: Which figure represents a one-way valve?
n: Figure E is a swing check valve, which allows flow one way only.

q: What jointing method is commonly used for HDPE pipes?
n: Polyethylene can't be solvent-welded.

q: HDPE stands for:
n: HDPE is a polyethylene.

q: What is the typical design life of HDPE pipe?
n: HDPE is rated for 50+ years, often quoted to 100.

q: Which statement about HDPE pipe is NOT true?
n: Its smooth bore gives good flow.

q: Which wells are dug with earth augers, are usually under 30 m deep, range from 2 to 30 in. in diameter, and are lined with metal, vitrified tile or concrete?
n: Augered wells are bored wells.

q: Which of the following is commonly used for water treatment (disinfection)?
n: Chlorination is the standard disinfection method for potable water.

q: What is installed to cut excessive water pressure at a fixture?
n: A PRV limits downstream pressure.

q: What is the minimum supply pipe size for a tank-type water closet?
n: Code tables give 1/2 in. for a tank-type WC.

q: What color identifies pipes carrying water?
n: Green is the identification color for water.

q: Which material should NOT be used for a pressurized water main?
n: Clay pipe is for gravity drainage only.

q: Which pipe is NOT recommended for a water line?
n: Lead contaminates drinking water.

q: Copper tubing comes in what forms?
n: Type K and L come in both tempers.

q: Which pipe is vulnerable to UV rays?
n: Sunlight embrittles PVC.

q: What is the main disadvantage of GI pipe in plumbing?
n: Zinc wears off and the pipe rusts and scales.

q: Which pipe is common for underground water lines because it doesn't corrode, but is brittle, has limited pressure rating and weak joints?
n: PVC fits the description.

q: Which describes PPR pipes used locally for water lines?
o: Resists chemicals, corrosion and high temperatures
n: PPR handles both hot and cold lines.

q: What valve in a curb box shuts off a building's water supply in emergencies, turned with a key?
n: The curb stop sits in the service line near the curb.

q: Which valve lets water flow in one direction only?
n: Check valves block reverse flow.

q: Which valve is installed right after the water meter?
n: A gate valve lets the line be shut off after the meter.

q: Which valve controls both temperature and flow in a shower?
n: Thermostatic valves mix to a set temperature.

q: Which valve is commonly used to open, close and throttle flow in a pipeline?
n: Globe valves are built for throttling.

q: Why are water supply pipes resized in high-rise buildings?
o: To handle the pressure difference between the service and the fixtures
n: Static head changes with height.

q: Where is water pressure highest in a plumbing system?
n: Static pressure rises with depth.

q: What mainly affects water pipe sizing in a multi-story building?
n: Height drives pressure loss and demand.

q: What is the main reason for increasing pipe size in a supply system?
n: Bigger pipes carry more flow at lower friction.

q: Which part of Metro Manila does Manila Water serve?
n: Manila Water holds the East Zone concession.

q: Which part of Metro Manila does Maynilad serve?
n: Maynilad holds the West Zone.

q: Which material is NOT recommended for rooftop water tanks?
n: Galvanized tanks rust and taint water.

q: What is the minimum distance between a water well and a sewer line or septic tank?
n: The Plumbing Code requires 15.2 m (50 ft).

q: Which of these valves is NOT meant for regulating flow?
n: Gate valves should be fully open or closed.

q: Which linear-motion valve is used to regulate water flow?
n: Globe valves have a linear stem; ball and butterfly are quarter-turn.

q: How are HDPE pipes joined?
n: HDPE is fusion welded.

q: How are PPR pipes joined?
n: PPR is socket-fused with a heating tool.

q: How are PVC pipes joined?
n: Solvent cement fuses the surfaces.

q: How are hubless cast iron pipes joined?
o: Neoprene couplings with stainless band clamps
n: No-hub couplings clamp the pipe ends.

q: Which flexible plastic tubing is suitable for hot and cold pressure lines and resists acids and alkalis but not fuel oil, gasoline or kerosene?
n: That is the textbook description of PB.

q: Which practice is illegal?
o: Providing a cistern to supply the building
Feeding each building's cistern from the main
Using a booster pump to draw water straight from the main
n: Pumping directly off the main robs pressure from neighbors.

q: What valve is typically installed where the service line enters, to shut off the whole building?
n: A full-port gate valve is the main shutoff.

q: What is the greenish film that forms on copper over time?
n: Patina is copper carbonate.

q: Which hand tool is used to flare tubing?
n: A flaring tool spreads the tube end.

q: Which valve gives the finest flow control?
n: A tapered needle meters small flows.

q: What tool removes burrs inside a cut pipe?
n: Reaming restores the full bore.

q: What valve at a tank outlet or pump suction prevents backflow?
n: A foot valve is a check valve at the suction end.
